title: Update to External Distributor Rebate Program
raw_text:
Update to External Distributor Rebate Program
Category: Market Data and Connectivity; Alert 2026-022
Overview On September 1, 2026, IEX Exchange launched a new rebate program for Market Data Distributors. As described below, pending effectiveness of an SEC rule filing, IEX is expanding the program to apply to Extranet Providers who enlist new Data Subscribers in the same way the program applies to Data Subscribers. External Distributor Rebate Program As described in Trading Alert 2026-12 , IEX Exchange launched an External Distributor Rebate Program on September 1, 2026. Under the program, a Data Subscriber can earn a rebate equal to 75% of the subscription fees a new External Data Subscriber pays IEX for Real-Time IEX market data products (TOPS, DEEP, and DEEP+) it subscribes to through that Data Subscriber. IEX has expanded the External Distributor Rebate Program to also apply to Extranet Providers who enlist new Data Subscribers to subscribe to Real-Time IEX market data products. To qualify, an Extranet Provider must: opt into the program via an updated Extranet Addendum to the Connectivity Services Agreement; report to IEX each month any new Data Subscribers that began subscribing through it during the prior month; and ensure that each new Data Subscriber executes the IEX Data Subscriber Agreement. Only Data Subscribers who were not entitled to receive Real-Time IEX market data products as of July 1, 2026 count toward the rebate; it does not apply to an Extranet Provider’s existing customers. The rebate expires on the earlier of (a) the termination of the External Data Subscriber’s or Data Subscriber’s subscription or (b) August 31, 2028. title: Exemption of Debt Obligations Issued by the European Union Under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 for Purposes of Trading Futures Contracts on Those Securities
raw_text:
Exemption of Debt Obligations Issued by the European Union Under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 for Purposes of Trading Futures Contracts on Those Securities

The Securities and Exchange Commission (the "Commission" or the "SEC") is proposing an amendment to designate debt obligations issued by the European Union as "exempted securities" for the purposes of marketing and trading futures contracts on those securities in the United States or to U.S. persons. The amendment is designed to permit futures trading on debt obligations issued by the European Union to be regulated as futures on "exempted securities," subject to the Commodity Exchange Act. The proposal is intended to increase U.S. persons' access to the market for these products, which may improve opportunities for hedging; lower transaction costs; contribute to greater market depth; reduce operational friction; and increase competition.

NYSE Options: Professional Customer Order Review Period Update
Markets: NYSE AMERICAN OPTIONS, NYSE ARCA OPTIONS; Services: Trading, Post Trade, Market Data
NYSE Arca Options and NYSE American Options have amended their respective 'Definitions - Customer and Professional Customer' rules (NYSE Arca Rule 1, NYSE American Rule 900.2NY) to require Member Firms to review customer activity on a monthly basis, rather than quarterly, to determine whether orders that are not for the account of a Broker or Dealer should be represented as Professional Customer orders. Orders for any non-Broker/Dealer customer that had an average of more than 390 orders per day during a calendar month must be represented as Professional Customer orders for the following calendar month. Member Firms are required to make any appropriate changes to the way in which they are representing such orders within five days after the end of each calendar month. This amendment became effective July 1, 2026. Please contact rmteam@nyse.com with any questions about this update.

MIAX Sapphire — Trading Alert, Technical Alert — MIAX Sapphire Options Exchange - Updated MEO Interface Specifications to Support Upcoming Aggregate Risk Manager (ARM) Origin Multiplier Enhancement
Trading Alert, Technical Alert MIAX Sapphire September 03, 2026 | 04:01 PM MIAX Sapphire Options Exchange - Updated MEO Interface Specifications to Support Upcoming Aggregate Risk Manager (ARM) Origin Multiplier Enhancement The MIAX Sapphire Options Exchange MIAX Express Order (MEO) Interface Specification has been updated to support the Aggregate Risk Manager (ARM) Origin Multiplier enhancement. MEO Interface Specification v1.3: Aggregate Risk Manager (ARM) Origin Multiplier Functionality This optional feature allows Market Makers to configure an “ARM Origin Multiplier” for each contra-side origin type. The multiplier will be applied to each ARM-eligible trade size based on the contra-side origin type, allowing Market Makers to set up ARM profiles so that trades against certain origin types are weighted differently than others in the MM Trade Percentage Calculation. Note: Current settings will extend to all contra-types at 100% weightings by default for firms using existing application protocols. Updates to the MEO Interface Specification are as follows: ARM Origin Multiplier Functionality ARM Origin Multiplier related fields added and “Message Type” change to RS in Simple ARM Settings Update Request ARM Origin Multiplier related fields added in ARM Simple Settings Update Response ARM Origin Multiplier related fields added and “Message Type” change to RN in Simple ARM Protection Settings Notification Additional Details: The new features are pending SEC approval and an activation schedule and will be announced in a future alert. The new features will be available in the MIAX Sapphire Option Exchange Firm Test Bed (FTB2) environment on October 20, 2026. Visit MIAX Sapphire Options Interface Specifications for additional details. For additional information, please contact MIAX Trading Operations at TradingOperations@miaxglobal.com or (609) 897-7302.

MIAX Emerald — Trading Alert, Technical Alert — MIAX Exchange Group - Options Exchanges - Planned Network Switch Hardware Refresh for CH4 (Disaster Recovery) Edge Switches and Mandatory Testing
Trading Alert, Technical Alert MIAX Emerald September 04, 2026 | 11:59 AM MIAX Exchange Group - Options Exchanges - Planned Network Switch Hardware Refresh for CH4 (Disaster Recovery) Edge Switches and Mandatory Testing On Friday, September 25, 2026, the MIAX Options, MIAX Pearl Options, MIAX Emerald Options and MIAX Sapphire Options Exchanges will refresh customer facing CH4 (Disaster Recovery) extranet edge switches after the close of trading from 5:30 p.m. - 9:30 p.m. ET. All of MIAX Options Exchanges CH4 extranet edge switches will be replaced one-to-one with an updated model and all firm Cross Connects (CCs) will be moved to the same ports on the new switches. There are no changes required by firms for this hardware upgrade. Following the upgrade, firms are required to verify all MIAX Options, Pearl Options, Emerald Options and Sapphire Options Exchanges cross connects, market data feeds and application logins. Please note: This testing is scheduled to coincide with the 2026 SIFMA pre-testing date to minimize operational disruptions. Details on testing and verifications: Testing will be held on Saturday, September 26, 2026, from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon ET. Firms are required to perform the following verifications: Verify light levels and IP routing. Verify all 10G ULL and 1G LL CCs by logging into each subscribed application for each CC (i.e. establish application-level socket connections to MEI, MEO, FOI, CTD, etc., for all ports, across all CCs) and verify the login. Confirm heartbeat receipt for both the A & B market data feeds for all subscribed multicast feeds across each CC. After verifying connectivity, firms must email MIAX Trading Operations at TradingOperations@miaxglobal.com . Please contact MIAX Trading Operations at TradingOperations@miaxglobal.com or (609) 897-7302 to arrange testing or to receive additional information on the planned network refresh.

title: C5. When must the value ‘O’ (Market Making) be used for accountHolderType?
raw_text:
C5. When must the value ‘O’ (Market Making) be used for accountHolderType?

For CAT reporting purposes, the accountHolderType value of market maker (value ‘O’) is used to identify orders originated by registered market makers, or Industry Members displaying quotes on an IDQS, including instances where an Industry Member is indirectly quoting on an IDQS by using the anonymous feature of an ATS, in their market making account. The value of ‘O’ must be used for all activity in the Industry Member’s market making account for a security in which it is registered, regardless of where the order is ultimately routed or executed, or whether the activity is directly related to maintenance of an Industry Member’s market making obligations. For example, block facilitation and hedging activity in the market making account in a security the Industry Member is a registered market maker must also be reported as ‘O’.

Because options market making is currently defined and identified through use of the OCC clearing range, a separate CAT reporting guideline for the use of the accountHolderType of 'O’ for options orders has been mandated.

The accountHolderType value of 'O’ is not intended to identify all forms of market making under various rules, such as short sales rules, Volcker, etc. Further, it is not intended to identify all trading in any proprietary account that may be used for market making activity, including hedging activity in securities for which an Industry Member is not a registered market maker or block positioning in securities for which the Industry Member is not a registered market maker. It is also not intended to identify proprietary activity in securities in which an Industry Member is registered as a market maker that originate from desks other than the market making desk. For example, activity occurring on a program desk that is walled off from the market making desk in securities that an Industry Member is a registered market maker must be marked with an ‘accountHolderType’ value of ‘P’ (Other Proprietary).

Specifically:

For CAT reporting purposes only, the accountHolderType value 'O' (Market Making) must be used as follows:

Simple Equities: The value 'O' must be used for any order originated in an Industry Member’s market making account in a security for which the Industry Member is registered as a market maker, designated market maker, lead market maker or similar capacity on a national securities exchange or in which the Industry Member displays quotations on an IDQS in an unlisted stock. This includes instances where an Industry Member is indirectly quoting on an IDQS by using the anonymous feature of an ATS.

Simple Options: The value 'O' must be used for any order originated in an account of the Industry Member that clears in the OCC clearing range of 'M'.

Complex Options: The value ‘O’ must be used for any order originated in an account of the Industry Member where the option leg(s) clear(s) in the OCC clearing range of ‘M’. 

See FAQ B68 for more information on how to populate the accountHolderType field if an Industry Member uses the same account for both market making and non-market making proprietary activity.

title: B68. If an Industry Member uses the same account for both market making and non-market making proprietary activity, what accountHolderType must be used when reporting to CAT?
raw_text:
B68. If an Industry Member uses the same account for both market making and non-market making proprietary activity, what accountHolderType must be used when reporting to CAT?

For order events (new order, new quote, trade and fulfillment events), if an Industry Member uses the same account for both market making and non-market making proprietary activity, the accountHolderType must be populated on an order-by-order basis. Orders meeting the definition of market making activity pursuant to FAQ C5 must be reported with the accountHolderType of 'O'. All other orders must be reported with the accountHolderType of 'P'.

Per FAQ U5, allocations to firm owned or controlled accounts are not required to be reported but may optionally be reported. For allocation events (post-trade allocation and amended allocation events) that are being optionally reported, if the Industry Member’s system is able to determine the accountHolderType on an allocation-by-allocation basis, the same guidance applies: allocations related to orders meeting the definition of market making activity pursuant to FAQ C5 must be reported with the accountHolderType of 'O' and allocations related to all other orders must be reported with the accountHolderType of 'P'. However, if the Industry Member’s system is unable to determine if the allocation is related to an order that was market making or non-market making proprietary activity, the Industry Member must populate the accountHolderType on its allocation events with the allowable value ('P' or 'O') according to its books and records.

title: Political Contributions by Certain Investment Advisers
raw_text:
Political Contributions by Certain Investment Advisers

The Securities and Exchange Commission (the "Commission" or the "SEC") is proposing to rescind the political contribution rule under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (the "Advisers Act"), which prohibits investment advisers from providing investment advisory services for compensation to a government client for two years after an adviser or any covered associate of the adviser makes a contribution to certain categories of elected officials or candidates, among other prohibitions. In the more than fifteen years since the rule was adopted, implementation challenges associated with the political contribution rule have resulted in a range of significant unintended consequences, including compliance practices among some investment advisers that may have had the effect of restricting all political contributions by the investment advisers and their employees. Market participants also have stated that the political contribution rule is burdensome, complex, and both lacks clarity and creates a de facto strict liability standard. The Commission is of the view that other existing requirements of the Advisers Act and its associated rules, including prohibitions on fraud, fiduciary duty requirements, the compliance rule, and the code of ethics rule (defined below), are likely sufficient to address pay-to-play practices while allowing an adviser the flexibility to implement an approach that is more appropriately tailored to its particular risks, rendering the political contribution rule unnecessary. The Commission also is proposing to amend the rule under the Advisers Act pertaining to books and records consistent with the proposed rescission.

Clearing Alert, Trading Alert MIAX Futures September 10, 2026 | 04:29 PM MIAX Futures Exchange - Onyx Trading Platform and Clearing System - FIA Disaster Recovery Pre-Test and 2026 Test MIAX Futures Exchange will participate in the industry-wide Futures Industry Association (“FIA”) sponsored Disaster Recovery (“DR”) pre-test on Saturday, September 26, 2026 and test on Saturday, October 24, 2026. U.S. futures exchanges, clearing houses, futures commission merchants, back-office providers, and data vendors will test connectivity and functionality between DR sites. All MIAX Futures Clearing Members are required to participate in both the Pre-Test and Test. Failure to participate as required may result in disciplinary action. Although your firm may work with a technology vendor to complete required test components, each Clearing Member is responsible for certification of final test results. September 26, 2026: Pre-Test Connectivity Pre-Test on Saturday, September 26, 2026: Onyx Trading Platform: MIAX Futures DR connections will be available from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. CT. Firms, data vendors, and clearing members may test connections to the Onyx trading platform during that time. MIAX Futures Clearing: To test connectivity, all Clearing Members must connect and download any previous TREX file from the MIAX Futures DR SFTP detailed below, using regular production credentials, any time between 8:00 a.m. and 12:00 p.m. CT. MIAX Futures SFTP will be failed over during testing to the Production IP Address 2 listed in the SFTP request form. Firms may test this connection at any time leading up to the test as it is always available. Required Responses: Please contact MIAX Future Clearing at (612) 321-7146 or MIAXFuturesClearingOperations@miaxglobal.com by Monday, September 21, 2026 , to confirm your participation in the pre-test. Please include a contact name, email and phone number for the pre-test. Once testing is completed, send an email to MIAXFuturesClearingOperations@miaxglobal.com noting if testing was successful or details of any issues. October 24, 2026: Test Script Clearing Members must complete the following four test components during the DR test: Trade Entry – MIAX Futures Onyx Trading Platform All Clearing Members must send at least two orders and receive at least one Commodities execution confirmation. Additionally, all Clearing Members with connections to Financial Futures Trading Platform (NY5), must send at least two orders and receive at least one Financial Futures execution confirmation. Products: Hard Red Spring Wheat Futures (MWE) i.e. MWEZ6 Hard Red Spring Wheat Options (OMW) i.e. OMWZ6 C0750 Bloomberg 100 Index (TBQ) i.e. TBQZ26 Bloomberg 500 Index (TBX) i.e. TBXZ26 Prices in MIAX Futures products should be entered at the previous day’s settlement price to ensure your orders match with other participants. October 24, 2026 Test Day Timeline: 7:30 a.m. CT – Firms can connect to the Trading Systems 7:45 a.m. CT – Live Order Window (LOW) First Pre-Opening 8:30 a.m. CT – Opening 12:00 p.m. CT – Closing MIAX Futures will provide updates as to exact pre-open and open times via the FIA conference bridge available. Once a firm has completed Onyx match engine testing, please confirm with MIAX Futures Trading Operations at MIAXFuturesTradingOperations@miaxglobal.com . Trade Entry – MIAX Futures Clearing System (MCS) I n addition to entering trades on Onyx, Clearing Members must enter an ex-pit transaction (EFP/EFR/Block) via MCS. Clearing Members should simply enter both sides of the transaction to ensure a successful match occurs in MCS for this portion of the test. Hard Red Spring Wheat Futures (W) i.e. W 12 26 (commodity, month, year) Hard Red Spring Wheat Options (WC or WP) i.e. WC 12 26 750 (comm., mth, yr, strike) Clearing Members should use October 24 for the trade date. Post Trade Documentation – Retrieve MIAX Futures TREX Trade File Trades entered into Onyx and MCS during the exercise will be processed by the MIAX Futures Clearing House, and Clearing Members must download the corresponding TREX trade file. Clearing Members will utilize the MIAX Futures DR SFTP server to retrieve the TREX files. The trade file name will correspond with the new convention being used today, i.e. – TRXzz_yyyymmdd.txt (where zz equates to the Clearing Firm code & yyyymmdd equals trade date). Post Trade Documentation – Submit to MIAX Futures After completing the above steps, Clearing Members must submit the SFTP file available via the MIAX Futures DR SFTP site to MIAX Futures by emailing MIAXFuturesClearingOperations@miaxglobal.com . Upon submitting, MIAX Futures staff will inform the Clearing Member whether they have successfully completed the FIA DR test for MIAX Futures or if further action is required. MIAX Futures Testing Contacts For more information and/or test day inquiries, please contact the MIAX Futures Clearing House at MIAXFuturesClearingOperations@miaxglobal.com or (612) 321-7146. Staff will be monitoring the FIA Conference Bridge phone for any inquiries. For questions relating to MIAX Futures Onyx, please contact MIAXFuturesTradingOperations@miaxglobal.com . To learn more about MIAX Futures, please contact MIAXFutures@miaxglobal.com . To register or revise MIAX Futures Alert subscriptions, visit MIAX Email Subscriptions .
